page.layout: One page of text in one column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Paragraphs begin with numbers 1 to 5, with Greek quotations in the text. Signature at the foot left, and the start of paragraph 5 on the last line.

main_text.p: 1. Direptio facultatum. Hostes enim sacra & profana pro sua libidine ἀγῶσι ἀλλὰ φόβοι[?]. Expugnatis Sardibus à Cyro, Irus & est subito, qui modo Croesus erat. Quàm sit hoc malum honestis hominibus graue, ex Menandri monosticho liquet: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡδὺ ἀνὴρ ἀτιμίαν [illegible, ~6 letters] ποιεῖ, & ex illo versu Euripidis: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡδὺ ἀνὴρ ἀνδρὸς ἀνυβρὶς [?] ἀνήρ.
2. Promiscuae cædes. Trucidantur omnium ordinum homines, ac inprimis iij qui patriae praesidio & ornamento ef-se[?] videntur.

3. Provinciarum occupatio. Vt Cam byses victo Psammeticho, & interfecto eius filio, Ægyptum Perfarū imperio subij-cit. Paulus Æmilius, debellato captoq; Perseo, Macedoniæ regnum in provin-ciam populi Romani convertit.

4. Vrbium expugnatio. Sæpe urbes κατὰ κράτος expugnatæ & captæ, funditus euertuntur: ut Hierosolyma à Tito, Vespasiani Imp. F. solo æquata est, sicut Dominus IESVS futurum prædixerat. Eadem urbs sancta iam antea à Babylonijs, usu Nebucadnezaris, incesa fuit & deleta.

page.notes: Greek passages are only partly legible in the scan and are marked [?] or [illegible]. The ornament "ef-se" at the line break is doubtful. "Quàm" keeps the printed grave accent. "Perfarū" and "Pfammeticho" are kept as printed; "Psammeticho" is the usual spelling.
